analysis: The method addListener receives an InvalidationListener parameter and calls listeners.add(listener) without any prior validation or checks. The listeners field is presumed to be a List or similar collection. The context does not include any explicit checks for null, type compatibility, list mutability, or other properties. Therefore, all declared exceptions of the add method remain possible: UnsupportedOperationException (if the list does not support add), ClassCastException (if the listener class prevents addition), NullPointerException (if listener is null and the list disallows nulls), and IllegalArgumentException (if some property of the listener prevents addition). None of these exceptions are avoided by the calling code.
answer:
UnsupportedOperationException: Not avoided - No check for list mutability.
ClassCastException: Not avoided - No type check before adding.
NullPointerException: Not avoided - No null check on the parameter.
IllegalArgumentException: Not avoided - No property validation.
remark: The exceptions are not avoided because the calling code does not perform any validation or conditional handling. For example, if the listeners collection is unmodifiable, add will throw UnsupportedOperationException. If the listener is null and the list does not allow null elements, NullPointerException is thrown. Similarly, a custom list implementation may throw ClassCastException or IllegalArgumentException based on the element's type or properties. Since the code does not prevent these scenarios, all four exceptions can still occur at runtime.
